Answer: A
Reason: The chest radiograph shows near-complete opacification (white-out) of the right hemithorax with a distinct contralateral (leftward) mediastinal shift, which is the classic presentation of a massive pleural effusion pushing structures away from the affected side. In contrast, atelectasis would cause an ipsilateral shift toward the opacity, and pneumothorax would present as hyperlucency rather than white-out.
